speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I notice you have yellowing of the skin and eyes and seem agitated; how long have these symptoms been present? Have you experienced any abdominal pain, fever, or changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior, have you experienced any fever, right-sided abdominal pain, or nausea recently? I also need to check if you have any recent exposure to new sexual partners or unprotected contact.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the combination of jaundice, agitation, and high-risk sexual behavior, I need to rule out acute hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis A, B, and C serology; Liver Function Tests.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal viral hepatitis serologies and severe liver dysfunction suggest a toxic or metabolic cause, possibly related to your substance use. Have you taken any acetaminophen, consumed wild mushrooms, or used any other recreational drugs in the past week?

text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Occasional use of cocaine and ecstasy. Social alcohol consumption (about 20 g on weekends).

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you deny acetaminophen or mushroom ingestion, have you consumed any herbal supplements, energy drinks, or new recreational substances recently that might be hepatotoxic? I also need to ask if you have noticed any dark, tea-colored urine or pale, clay-colored stools, which would indicate obstructive jaundice.

speaker: Patient
text: The patient shows signs of psychomotor agitation and confusion. No other symptoms provided.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the severe coagulopathy (INR 1.5, TP <40%) and high bilirubin with negative viral markers, this suggests acute liver failure likely from a toxin or metabolic cause. REQUEST TEST: Acetaminophen level, serum tox screen, autoimmune hepatitis panel, ceruloplasmin.
